evidence_classes.PRESENCE_EVIDENCE: A dated and geographically attributable observation supports presence at that place and time only.
evidence_classes.LOCAL_PEAK: Repeated observations support a productivity peak only for the monitored site, years and protocol.
evidence_classes.BOUNDARY_NOT_AUTHORIZED: The evidence does not support a complete biological season boundary or absence outside observed dates.

prohibitions: Do not infer absence from presence-only data.
Do not convert a legal collection window into biological phenology.
Do not generalize a local peak to all of Italy.
Do not use this artifact as an overall-v2 gate, cap, veto or weight.
Do not use confidence as biological favourability.

gbif_snapshot.interpretation: Aggregated presence-only observations. Counts are not sampling effort and months without records are not absences.

published_evidence.citation: Salerni E, Perini C, Gardin L. Linking Climate Variables with Tuber borchii Sporocarps Production. Natural Resources 5 (2014): 408-418.
published_evidence.territory: Marina di Alberese, Grosseto, Tuscany, Italy
published_evidence.protocol: Five natural production areas; weekly trained-dog surveys from January through April in 1996-1999; fruitbodies morphologically identified, counted, weighed, measured and recorded.
published_evidence.local_peak: February-March in the monitored areas and years
limitations: No surveys from May through December.

published_evidence.citation: Vita F et al. Environmental conditions influence the biochemical properties of the fruiting bodies of Tuber magnatum Pico. Scientific Reports 8 (2018).
published_evidence.territory: Multiple sites in Tuscany, Marche, Piedmont, Molise and Abruzzo, plus Croatia
published_evidence.protocol: Mature fruitbodies sampled during the second half of November in 2014 and 2015 at 17 sites.
limitations: Targeted mature-sample collection, not year-round monitoring.
Cannot establish start, end or absence boundaries.

published_evidence.citation: Mello A et al. Spatio-Temporal Dynamic of Tuber magnatum Mycelium in Natural Truffle Grounds. PLOS ONE 9 (2014).
published_evidence.protocol: Repeated soil/mycelium study with public supplementary analysis dataset and dates for associated ascomata.
limitations: Primary target is mycelium rather than systematic fruitbody phenology.

published_evidence.citation: Vita F et al. Volatile organic compounds in truffle fruiting bodies from Alba and San Miniato. Scientific Reports 5 (2015).
published_evidence.protocol: Targeted summer (June-August) and autumn/winter (October-December) fruitbody groups across 2011-2013.
limitations: Targeted biochemical sampling, not systematic year-round effort.
Summer fruitbody presence must not be equated with legal harvestability or commercial maturity.

published_evidence.citation: Pacioni G et al. Instrumental monitoring of the birth and development of truffles in a Tuber melanosporum orchard. Mycorrhiza 24 Suppl 1 (2014): 65-72.
published_evidence.protocol: Instrumental orchard monitoring of soil and atmospheric parameters since 2009, with observation of primordia development.
limitations: Development observations do not authorize a national mature-fruitbody boundary.

published_evidence.citation: Egli S et al. The fall of the summer truffle: recurring hot, dry summers result in declining fruitbody production of Tuber aestivum in Central Europe. Global Change Biology (2022).
published_evidence.protocol: Twenty sites, 2011-2018, 1,781 surveys and 6,633 fruitbodies at approximately three-week resolution.
limitations: Supports climate sensitivity and site variability, not an Italian boundary.

runtime_decision.required_behavior: Keep phenology-v1 fail-closed where no separately authorized claim-bound rule exists.
